assets.title: Chopin — Nocturne Op.9 No.2 — Frank Levy, piano
assets.provider: Musopen, "Set Chopin Free" Kickstarter project (performer: Frank Levy) -- recorded specifically to be released public domain, not an incidental amateur upload
assets.license: Public domain (Musopen "Set Chopin Free"; the composition itself, by Chopin, 1832, is public domain everywhere too) — no credit required.
assets.character: REPLACES an earlier IMSLP amateur recording (Harald Vetter) pulled 20 Oct 22:50 PDT -- Jackie, having listened: "there are literally wrong notes." This Levy/Musopen recording correlates r=0.982 (pitch-class histogram, scripts/music-verify/) against the pulled recording, meaning no evidence of a different or badly mangled performance -- NOT proof of zero wrong notes; a handful of wrong pitches barely moves a histogram. Trimmed, normalized to -6.6 dBFS peak to match the score's own level, 2s fade-out. Second member of the early-play rotation pool alongside `human` (see audio.mjs HUMAN_POOL) -- Liebestraum, the third member, is pulled pending a better-verified recording.
assets.edit: Trimmed 1.9s lead-in (from a measured 2.0s) and 1.4s trailing dead air (from a measured 1.6s), 0.6s linear fade-out added at the new end; no gain change (source already had ample headroom at -1.71 dBFS peak); AAC transcode only otherwise. Not independently listened to -- see report.

assets.title: Satie — Gymnopédie No.1 — Robin Alciatore, piano
assets.provider: Musopen (performer: Robin Alciatore) -- a dedicated professional-recording project, not an incidental amateur upload
assets.license: Public domain (Musopen; the composition itself, by Satie, 1888, is public domain everywhere too) — no credit required.
assets.character: REPLACES an earlier IMSLP amateur recording (Luis Kolodin) pulled 20 Oct 22:50 PDT alongside Liebestraum and the Chopin nocturne. This Alciatore/Musopen recording correlates r=0.95-0.99 (pitch-class histogram, scripts/music-verify/) against FOUR independent recordings including the pulled one, meaning no evidence of a different or badly mangled performance across any of them -- NOT proof of zero wrong notes in any one; a handful of wrong pitches barely moves a histogram. Trimmed, normalized to -6.6 dBFS peak to match the score's own level, 2s fade-out. `departure`'s one-way handoff target after one full loop of its own ending theme on the win screen (see audio.mjs).
assets.edit: Trimmed 2.5s of trailing dead air past the final decay, 0.6s linear fade-out added; no gain change (already has ample headroom at −6 dBFS peak); AAC transcode only otherwise. Not independently listened to — see report.
